title: BGNN 2D + snout
note: Started as a copy of BGNN 2D body landmarks (23) and diverges from it as soon as a landmark is added, so its files are not that protocol's files.
landmarks: The forward-most point of the lower jaw's dentary bone.
The back corner of the mouth, where the jaws meet.
The front edge of the bony eye socket, not of the pupil.
The back edge of the bony eye socket.
The top edge of the bony eye socket.
The bottom edge of the bony eye socket.
The middle of the eye socket, between the four limits.
The rear point of the supraoccipital crest, on the midline behind the skull roof.
Anteriormost base of the first dorsal-fin ray
Where the front edge of the first dorsal ray meets the body.
Posteriormost base of the last dorsal-fin ray
Where the back edge of the last dorsal ray meets the body.
Top of the crease left when the tail is flexed, at the caudal-fin base.
Compound vertebral centrum at posterior of vertebral column
The last vertebral centrum, at the end of the vertebral column.
Bottom of the crease at the caudal-fin base.
Posteriormost point of the base of the anal fin
Where the back of the anal-fin base meets the body.
Anteriormost base of the first anal-fin ray
Where the front edge of the first anal ray meets the body.
Posteriormost point of the base of the pelvic fin
Where the back of the pelvic-fin base meets the body.
Anteriormost point of the base of the pelvic fin
Where the front of the pelvic-fin base meets the body.
The upper corner where the pectoral fin leaves the body.
Innermost point of pectoral fin (bottom point)
The lower, inner corner of the pectoral-fin base.
The cleithrum's posterior margin, the bony ridge behind the gill opening.
The inner-most point of the gill cover's margin.
The top point of the gill cover.
The bottom point of the gill cover.
The front tip of the mouth: the forward-most point of the closed upper jaw. Snout length runs from here to the front of the orbit.
Dorsal end of the greatest body depth

The top of the body where it is deepest, measured at right angles to the snout-to-caudal line; on the body's edge, not on a fin or the scales at its base. With the next point it gives greatest body depth, compared with least caudal-peduncle depth (the caudal-crease points).
Ventral end of the greatest body depth
The bottom of the body straight across from the dorsal end, at right angles to the snout-to-caudal line.
